purpose: Machine-readable guardrail for hyperscaler, cloud-native, and Kubernetes-native lane work. This keeps active plans on controller reconciliation, Buck2/Prow evidence, trusted controller-owned required context, restricted workload security, generated shared surfaces, and shadow-only adapters while rejecting live-mutation shortcuts and retired bridge authorities.

official_sources.establishes: Cloud-native architectures favor loosely coupled, interoperable, observable, resilient services rather than shared mutable bottlenecks.
Kubernetes controllers reconcile observed state toward desired state through control loops.
Restricted Pod Security establishes least-privilege pod/container defaults for untrusted workloads.
NetworkPolicy supports pod traffic isolation and default-deny policy shape.
Kubernetes securityContext controls non-root execution, privilege escalation, read-only root filesystems, seccomp, and Linux capabilities.
RuntimeClass selects container runtime configuration for pod-level runtime isolation.
Pods can opt out of automatic ServiceAccount token mounting.
Draining evicts workloads through Kubernetes APIs instead of blind pod deletion.
ProwJob configuration is the compatible pattern input for presubmit, postsubmit, periodic, and batch CI jobs.

required_patterns.implementation_hook: Prow/Kubernetes-native controllers own desired-state reconciliation; local specs are static evidence only.
Only the trusted oya-ci controller rollup may publish the durable oya-ci-required context.
Buck2 targets remain the build/test/check authority; Cargo/Tarpaulin/local scripts are advisory unless projected into Buck2/Prow evidence.
CI workloads use workload identity, block node metadata access, and reject static cloud secrets.
Generated controller config requires no privilege escalation, read-only root filesystems, non-root users, RuntimeDefault seccomp, and dropped ALL capabilities.
Default-deny network policy is required before explicit lane-owned egress/ingress grants.
Untrusted PR jobs run through a sandboxed RuntimeClass and restricted runner ServiceAccount.
Service-to-service traffic records mTLS intent and must later bind to mesh identity before production claims.
Shared files stay pointer-thin or generated from lane-owned shards to reduce merge conflicts.
GitHub/GitHub Actions adapters remain temporary publication/shadow surfaces until native SCM/oya-ci/release conveyor cutover.
Pure-Rust-biased Sapling-inspired SCM owns change graph; oya-ci owns Buck2/Prow execution; release-conveyor-like CD owns progressive delivery ledger.
Cloud and Oyatie product auth/shared substrates stay decoupled now to avoid shared contract conflicts; later product rewrites consume Cloud IdP.

forbidden_anti_patterns.rejects: Deleting pods directly as an operational plan instead of scaling, draining, pausing, or reconciling through controller-owned desired state.
A candidate PR, local script, or human-posted status acting as durable oya-ci-required truth.
Treating GitHub Actions as permanent first-class CI/CD authority instead of temporary compatibility/shadow evidence.
Jenkins, Forgejo, ArgoCD, Argo Workflows/Rollouts, or retired Oya CLI gates as active interim authority.
One shared hand-edited CI workflow as the coordination surface for parallel product/infra/cloud lanes.
New durable gate/check surfaces in Python or shell instead of Rust libraries, Buck2 targets, and Prow/Kubernetes jobs.
Reviving oya vcs, oya git, oya gate, or oya verify as sanctioned merge/CI authority.
Letting Cargo, Tarpaulin, or ad-hoc local tools outrank Buck2-native LLVM coverage and Buck2 check authority.
Allowing CI or service pods to reach node metadata APIs for cloud credentials.
Implicitly mounting default ServiceAccount tokens in CI/workload pods.
Privileged containers, privilege escalation, writable root filesystems, root execution, or retained Linux capabilities as defaults.
Running untrusted PR jobs without a sandboxed RuntimeClass.
Relying on open pod networking instead of default-deny plus explicit grants.
